problems.problem: The signature event - a floor shade whose outline narrows and bends into the contour curve ('影子先到,曲线随后') - still renders as a straight, symmetric vertical smudge under the base (visible y≈1050-1330, centered on x≈712). In image 1 and the contact crop [543,905,883,1155] the shade tapers uniformly with no S-bend or contour waist, so it reads as a glossy-floor reflection of the bottle, not a shaped shadow guest arriving first. Contact itself is correct (base_y 1045 meets the shade with no gap), so this is a form failure, not a grounding failure.
problems.root_cause: The regenerated cyclorama delivered the requested value structure but the diffuse floor shade kept a mirror-reflection geometry; prompt language alone has twice failed to produce a curved taper.
problems.repair_strategy: Regenerate the empty set with a prompt that forbids mirror reflection and states the floor shade as an off-axis, gently S-curved tapering form drifting toward the lower-left foreground; simultaneously add one deterministic background ellipse as a darker grey curved shade lobe so the contour bend is guaranteed by geometry, not only by prose.

problems.problem: The corrected mid-grey cyc now matches the source cutout's even front/above lighting (bright neck glass and white script no longer fight a charcoal wall), but the wall reads as a near-uniform light grey field with only corner vignetting; behind the 650px hero there is no luminance pool or gradient event, so the product column floats on flat value instead of being held by the set, unlike references 3-5 where one crafted light or color gesture anchors the hero.
problems.root_cause: Previous fix prioritized value match over sculpted light; the prompt's 'gentle even light across the whole surface' removed the pooling that would seat the bottle.
problems.repair_strategy: Regenerate with a soft radial luminance pool centered on the product column falling off toward the frame edges, keeping overall value close to the source backdrop and preserving the diffuse frontal overhead illumination description without naming equipment.

problems.problem: The enlarged subtitle (34pt, y≈886-918) and logo (42pt, tracking 4, y≈1037-1069) now read at poster distance, but the left column still has a dead band between the title foot (y≈724) and subtitle head (y≈886) of ~160px of empty grey, while subtitle-to-logo gap is ~119px; the three type steps therefore read as title-then-two-orphans rather than one composed vertical measure, and the dark ink sits on the lightest part of the floor transition where the subtitle's thin strokes lose edge crispness.
problems.root_cause: Size increases were applied without re-balancing vertical intervals; column rhythm still inherits the old page-scale spacing.
problems.repair_strategy: Tighten the column: move subtitle up toward y≈800 and logo up toward y≈980 so the three blocks form an even descending rhythm inside the reserved left band, keeping exact copy, left alignment and x=86.

problems.problem: References 3-5 each commit one dominant crafted gesture (sculpted liquid line work, staged color field with figure, splash crown). This poster's single gesture remains the unresolved straight smudge, so against those benchmarks the execution reads polished-draft: faithful cutout, calm believable set, confident type sizes, but the hero event that would lift it to professionally resolved is still missing.
problems.root_cause: Contrast budget is now correctly spent on a calm set, but the one intended high-craft element (contour shadow) has never been delivered in rendered form.
problems.repair_strategy: Solve via the combined prompt + deterministic ellipse patch in problem 1 so the curved shade becomes the visible crafted gesture, matching reference-level resolve without changing palette, genre or composition.
